matches.rationale: The ground truth identifies inflated performance claims in the abstract (2x-50x), while finding 2 claims the abstract understates the results. These are opposite distortions, not the same issue.
No finding addresses the inconsistent definition of network depth as Dense layers vs. discrete experimental depth levels.
No finding discusses undisclosed training regimes, learning rates, or compute budgets for deep networks up to 1024 layers.
No finding addresses the claim of qualitatively distinct emergent behaviors being supported only by limited humanoid visualizations.
No finding mentions the fabricated or unverifiable Neumann and Gros (2022) reference in Related Work.
No finding addresses the omitted limitations regarding compute requirements or environmental impact in the conclusion.
No finding identifies inflated promotional rhetoric in the abstract; finding 2 concerns the opposite direction of distortion.

Finding 5 identifies the same Figure 6 actor/critic scaling ablation as containing a text-figure inconsistency in the claimed impact of actor scaling, matching the ground truth's evidence-data integrity issue in the same section and figure.

Finding 4 directly addresses the batch size scaling claim: the text claims larger depth leverages batch size scaling while the same paragraph admits marginal or inconsistent improvements, matching the ground truth's narrative inconsistency about batch size and depth.
No finding discusses omitted ethical considerations such as carbon footprint, reproducibility costs, or societal implications.
No finding addresses the promotional claim in the introduction that depth scaling surpasses width scaling.
No finding mentions the unrealistic 983x improvement in Table 1 or inflated appendix performance numbers.
No finding identifies the L2-norm versus dot-product inconsistency in the critic output definition.
No finding addresses the MJX/Brax version discrepancy or its lack of disclosure in the main experimental section.
No finding discusses alternate methods like GCBC/GCSL and the over-crediting of CRL for depth scaling.
No finding addresses inconsistent wall-clock time values for depths beyond 64 in the appendix tables.
No finding addresses the overgeneralized claim that deep models exhibit qualitatively better behaviors interpreted as implicitly acquired skills.
